entry_point: Control-panel HTTP endpoints under /cp/navigation: page create/edit/validate, the navigation tree listing and save, and a navigation page preview

verified.entry_point: Confirmed offline at the pinned commit with the project's own Testbench harness: a CP user with only 'access cp' (or with 'view test nav' but no view right on the linked entry's collection) reads an entry's stored values back from the page-create request and from the page-edit request; the same user reads any navigation's title/URL/status from the navigation tree listing with no navigation permission at all, and a nav viewer who cannot view the linked entry reads that entry's title/URL/status/redirect from the tree. The tree save response and the preview endpoint disclose the same data (injected). All driven with real CP routes, real policies, real navs/trees/entries.

gate.blind: not present yet (written by the pipeline afterwards)

wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: the protection has no peer, direction or role dimension; the navigation right and the entry right are separate protections, each covered by its own tests rather than one toggle.
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: every protected sink is a read; the tree save is protected only through the data it returns, so there is no write counterpart whose guard could be omitted.
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: each request is gated before any value is produced, and the serializer's visibility test is evaluated before the entry-derived fields are emitted; there is no earlier normalisation of a caller value for a late check to be defeated by.
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: identities are entry IDs and navigation handles resolved by the product's own repositories; an unknown or malformed ID yields no entry or page rather than a different object to authorise.
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: authorisation is decided from the current user's own permissions by the project's policies; no external authority can return nothing and make a guard fail open.

traps.shape: the page editor's create/edit responses and the validate-only action; the linked entry arrives as a query parameter or as a stored branch reference, and its values appear both in the origin values and merged into the page values; the navigation object is site-scoped, so authorising the whole navigation instead of the site tree lets a user read another site
traps.reason_to_dismiss: none for the entry gate itself; the shape traps are that only the origin values look sensitive, and that the navigation looks like the object to authorise rather than its site-scoped tree

traps.shape: navigation tree listing with no navigation view gate: any authenticated CP user reads any navigation's page titles and addresses (a route where the protection never existed)
traps.reason_to_dismiss: it is the tree listing that feeds the navigation show page, and the show page is already gated, so it looks reachable only after that check

traps.shape: the tree serializer emits an entry's title, blueprint, URL, edit URL, slug, status, redirect and mounted collection for a nav viewer who may not view that entry; the producer is in another package and does check one permission already (can_delete), which makes the missing entry view check look intentional
traps.reason_to_dismiss: navigation viewers are expected to see the navigation's structure, so per-entry filtering reads as a feature change rather than an authorisation fix

traps.shape: the tree save endpoint builds and returns the refreshed tree, so the same serializer producer emits hidden entries through a second route that is gated only by the navigation edit right; a fix that filters the listing response (or the listing controller) leaves this open
traps.reason_to_dismiss: it is a write endpoint and the caller already holds the edit right for the navigation, so the response reads as part of the save result rather than a disclosure
traps.realistic_because: returning the refreshed tree from a save is a natural round-trip optimisation written in the same style as the listing action; injected into our copy only (environment/injection.patch), registered in build/audit/uncovered-routes.tsv

traps.shape: a read-only page preview endpoint returns the page's merged values (which include the linked entry's data), its title, URL and status with no navigation and no entry gate
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a read-only preview of a page the user is already editing looks harmless and is easy to treat as covered by the page editor's own fix
traps.realistic_because: a small read-only controller beside the page editor that merges the page and entry data the way the editor already does; injected into our copy only (environment/injection.patch), registered in build/audit/uncovered-routes.tsv
